Descent stage · ALSEP · LRV rover · flag · Duke family photo

The only mission to land in the lunar highlands. Charles Duke left a photo of his family sealed in a bag on the lunar surface. On the back he wrote: 'This is the family of Astronaut Duke from Planet Earth. Landed on the Moon, April 1972.' It will outlast civilisation.
Highland geological sampling — diversified the lunar sample inventory beyond mare basalts and reshaped models of planetary crust formation, methods reused for Mars.

Apollo 16 landed in the Descartes Highlands on April 21, 1972 — the only Apollo mission to a highland (not mare) site, chosen to sample what was believed to be volcanic terrain. Young and Duke found NO volcanic rocks — only impact breccias and anorthosite — overturning the geological model and demonstrating the Moon's highlands are an ancient impact-shattered crust, not later volcanism. Three EVAs, 27 km of LRV traverse, 95 kg of samples returned.
Apollo 16 crew portrait — John Young (CDR), Ken Mattingly (CMP — bumped from Apollo 13), Charlie Duke (LMP).
John Young leaping during the "Lunar Olympics" — first crewed lunar high-jump, demonstrating the 1/6 g.
Duke at "Big Muley" — sample 61016, the largest single rock returned from the Moon (11.7 kg).
